General.Description:
Kwame Asante left Accra at the age of fourteen with nothing but a school bag containing two textbooks, a change of clothes, and a letter of recommendation from a teacher who had seen something in him that Kwame himself could not yet see. He arrived in London six weeks later — via routes and in circumstances he does not describe in detail, and does not need to — speaking no English and knowing no one.

Twelve years later he graduated from the London School of Economics with a first-class degree in economics. Four years after that he founded an education access charity that has since placed over thirty thousand young people from refugee and asylum-seeking backgrounds into further education. He tells his own story with a directness and absence of self-pity that makes it more powerful than any dramatised account could be.

Against All Odds is not a book about suffering. It is a book about learning — how to learn, why learning matters, and what happens when you refuse to let any circumstance, however brutal, strip you of the right to become more than you are.

Asante writes with clarity, warmth, and occasional sharp humour. His voice is entirely his own.

Required reading for anyone who thinks the odds are fixed.
